examples.en: My account went into the minus.
The temperature dropped to minus five degrees.
This month the business is at a loss.

examples.ko: 급할 때를 위해 마이너스 통장을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I opened an overdraft account for emergencies.
That is not a disadvantage for us.
The calculation came out negative.

explain: 반대말은 '플러스'예요. 숫자 앞에 붙는 '-'뿐 아니라 돈이 모자라는 것, 손해, 도움이 안 되는 일에도 비유로 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 통장에 돈이 없어도 정해진 한도까지 빌려 쓸 수 있는 통장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An account that lets you borrow up to a set limit even with no balance.

explain_en: Its opposite is 플러스. Besides the "-" sign before a number, it is used figuratively for a shortage of money, a loss, or something unhelpful.

examples.en: I got overcharged at a restaurant in a tourist area.
In peak season, overcharging for lodging is serious.

examples.ko: 바가지요금인 줄 알았으면 안 샀을 거예요.
examples.en: If I had known it was a rip-off price, I wouldn't have bought it.

examples.ko: 바가지요금은 미리 가격을 물어보면 피할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can avoid rip-off prices by asking the price beforehand.

examples.ko: 바가지요금에 화가 나서 가게 주인에게 따졌어요.
examples.en: I was angry at the rip-off price and argued with the shop owner.

examples.ko: 바가지요금 때문에 휴가 기분이 다 망쳤어요.
examples.en: The inflated price ruined my whole vacation mood.

explain: 물건이나 서비스의 값이 정상보다 터무니없이 비쌀 때 써요. 보통 관광지, 택시, 성수기 숙박처럼 손님이 사정을 잘 모르는 상황에서 말해요. '바가지요금을 당하다/물다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 시장에서 물건을 샀다가 바가지를 써서 속상해요.
phrases.en: I bought something at the market and got ripped off, which upsets me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비싼 값을 속아서 내게 되었을 때 말해요. 반대로 상대가 그렇게 할 때는 '바가지를 씌우다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you were tricked into paying too much. When the seller does it to you, it is '바가지를 씌우다'.

explain_en: It is used when the price of goods or services is absurdly higher than normal. It is typically said in situations where the customer doesn't know the going rate, like tourist spots, taxis or peak-season lodging. Common patterns: '바가지요금을 당하다/물다'.

examples.en: Gas prices went up, so fuel costs a lot.
With an electric car, you hardly worry about fuel costs.
In winter, the burden of heating fuel costs is big.

examples.ko: 한 달 연료비를 계산해 보니 십만 원이에요.
examples.en: I calculated a month of fuel costs and it's 100,000 won.
The company covers fuel costs for business trips.

examples.ko: 연료비는 차가 클수록 더 많이 나와요.
examples.en: The bigger the car, the higher the fuel cost.

explain: '기름값'은 일상에서 주유할 때 편하게 하는 말이고, '연료비'는 차뿐 아니라 난방·운송 같은 비용 전체를 말할 때도 써요. '연료비가 들다', '연료비를 아끼다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '기름값' is the casual word for the price of gas when you fill up, while '연료비' can also cover costs for heating or transport in general. Typical phrases are '연료비가 들다' and '연료비를 아끼다'.

en: financial difficulty; stringency of capital; lack of funds

examples.en: The company closed because of a shortage of funds.
I heard the shop is having cash trouble.
Many small businesses suffer from a lack of funds.
The construction stopped halfway due to a funding shortage.
To solve the cash shortage, they borrowed money from a bank.
The funding crunch got so bad that even employees' pay was delayed.

explain: 회사나 가게 같은 곳의 운영 돈이 모자랄 때 써요. 개인 이야기라면 '돈이 없다', '쪼들리다'가 더 자연스러워요. '취업난', '구인난'처럼 '-난'이 붙은 말과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used when a company or shop runs short of operating money. For an individual, '돈이 없다' or '쪼들리다' sounds more natural. It helps to learn it with other '-난' words such as '취업난' and '구인난'.

examples.en: There are many low-wage jobs, so life is hard.

examples.ko: 저임금으로 일하는 사람도 최저임금은 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Even people who work for low wages must get at least the minimum wage.

examples.ko: 저임금 때문에 젊은 직원들이 회사를 떠나요.
examples.en: Young employees leave the company because of low pay.
Many young people are struggling with low pay.

examples.ko: 공장에서 저임금 노동자를 구한다는 공고가 났어요.
examples.en: A notice went up that the factory is looking for low-wage workers.
If low wages continue, spending drops too.

explain: 반대말은 '고임금'이에요. 일상에서는 '월급이 적다'라고 하고, 저임금은 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 더 많이 써요. '최저임금'은 법으로 정한 가장 낮은 금액이라서 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: The opposite is '고임금'. In daily talk people say '월급이 적다', while 저임금 appears more in news and economic discussion. '최저임금' is the legal minimum amount, so it means something different.
